title: The junior operator in her fourth month: one time offered, the booking taken, a summary without the address
purpose: Story S4, period P4. The booking is now hers to take: one time, said plainly, and a summary after it. The price still comes bare, the number is not read back, and a doubt about paying for a diagnosis is soothed instead of answered.

call.day: a working day of slot 6 in score period P4 (rule R6)

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller, Carla Jenkins, whose check engine light came on three days ago.
scenario.job: check engine light: scan, test and diagnose (one hour)
scenario.wants: somebody to look at it, and what that costs
scenario.what_happens: Maya asks whether the light is steady and how the car runs, takes the name and the number, gives the diagnostic price, soothes 'a hundred and thirty-five just to tell me what's wrong', offers tomorrow at ten, books it and repeats the time and the work.

facts.note: catalogue.json check_engine_diag: one hour at the posted rate, 135.00.

prices.what: Check engine light - scan, test & diagnose (1 hr)

script.said: Thanks for calling Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya. How can I help you?
Hi. My check engine light came on and I need somebody to look at it. What's that gonna cost me?
Okay, we can do that. What are you driving?
A twenty-fifteen Sonata.
Okay. And is the light staying on steady, or is it blinking at you?
It's just on. It's not blinkin'.
Okay, good — steady's better. Is the car driving any different? Like, is it shaking, or hesitating when you take off?
Not really. Maybe a little rough when it's sittin' still. It came on Monday.
Okay. Let me get your name real quick.
Carla Jenkins.
Carla Jenkins. And what's a good number for you, Carla?
Four two three, five five five, oh one five seven.
Okay, got it. So, Carla, the — what we do is hook it up and test it, and that's one thirty-five for the diagnostic.
Uh-huh.
A hundred and thirty-five dollars just to tell me what's wrong with it?
I know. I totally understand, it's — nobody likes paying for that part. But we'll take good care of you, I promise.
Hm. ...Okay.
So, um — I could get you in tomorrow at ten. Would that work?
I guess so. I gotta get it looked at.
Okay! So I've got you down for tomorrow, Friday, at ten, and I'll check you in myself.
Okay.
So that's tomorrow at ten for the check engine light on the Sonata.
Alright. Thanks.
Thank you, Carla! See you tomorrow.
Bye.

truth.note: The clean script earns the same levels.

why.greeting: 2: the business and her own name in the first line.
why.name_and_number: 1: she takes the name and the number and says 'got it' without saying the number back.
why.need_discovery: 2: the car, the job and what she asked for: steady, a little rough at idle, on since Monday.
why.price_with_next_step: 1: a price with nothing about what it covers or depends on; the time comes two of her lines later, after the doubt.
why.offered_time: 1: one specific option, tomorrow at ten.
why.asked_for_booking: 2: the day, the hour and who checks her in.
why.recap: 1: the time and the work; no address for a first-time customer.
why.objection: 1: the doubt is about paying to be told what is wrong, and it gets sympathy and a promise, not a reason. She books because she has to.
why.score: (1·2 + 2·1 + 2·2 + 2·1 + 3·1 + 3·2 + 1·1 + 2·1) / 2 = 11 of 16 weight points = 68.8. Exactly 68.75; the product rounds a score to one decimal.
